generated_from.note: The AES git commit is deliberately not embedded. The consumer pins the AES commit and this file's sha256.
generated_from.profile_version_semantics: <manifest_version>+<aes_commit>; the consumer supplies aes_commit from its own pin
generated_from.rule_refs_scope: rule_refs are the target/flow-fixed subset only. Axis and language profile files are resolved per request via axis_profile_paths / language_packs. Approved-example excerpts are never included.

schema.description: Optional, additive direction for the existing business magazine compiler and carousel renderer. It carries no publication authority.
schema.title: Carousel art direction plan

traits_applied.description: Which concrete audience.modality_effects.audio adjustments were actually applied to this plan, not the whole profile.

delivery_intent.description: Provider-neutral performance direction (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §12, §13) — augmented from register/audience, never an invented persona. Never SSML, audio tags, or provider syntax.

beat_id.description: Links to the shared argument-beat graph (editorial/VISUAL-STORY-COMPILATION.md §3). Required for audio/timed-narration — checked by scripts/lib/audio-plan-core.mjs.

speaker.description: Speaking role id for audio/dialogue segments; must resolve to one of dialogue.speaker_roles[].role_id.

selected_reference_traits.description: Traits only, never a reference body (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §2; editorial/profiles/reference/audio.json).

persona_disclosure.description: AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §15: a synthetic speaker may never be presented as a real source. The only value this schema accepts is the explicit non-source disclosure — any other value fails validation structurally.

schema.description: The pre-TTS contract (AES-V2.8 / SUE-566). Records the compiled canonical spoken script and every state a bad audio artifact must route back to — audience, artifact profile, reference traits, pronunciation, delivery, script L1 review — before an expensive render is attempted. Mirrors the lineage and gate structure of schemas/visual-job.schema.json rather than inventing a parallel one. See schemas/AUDIO-PLAN-CONTRACT.md.

artifact_profile.description: An audio artifact profile id from the artifact axis (editorial/profiles/axes.json, editorial/profiles/artifact/audio-*.json). The vocabulary is owned by that directory, not this enum (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §8 extension rule) — real membership is enforced by scripts/lib/audio-plan-core.mjs's UNKNOWN_PROFILE check against the directory, not by this pattern alone.

cost.description: Cost per accepted artifact, not raw render count (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §9).

dialogue.description: Required and validated only when artifact_profile is audio/dialogue (checked by scripts/lib/audio-plan-core.mjs, since this schema subset has no conditional keyword).

package_ref.description: Editorial Package reference, when this plan is compiled from a package rather than a single article. Exactly one of article_ref/package_ref must be present — checked by scripts/lib/audio-plan-core.mjs, not by this schema.

qa.description: Rendered-audio QA (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §20 'Render QA'). Structurally separate from script_l1 — a correct transcript certifies nothing about pronunciation, pacing, continuity, or performance.

recompilation.description: Evidence that the article was recompiled for listening rather than sent to TTS as-is (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §1). Required so skipping this step is structurally visible.

identical_to_source_prose.description: Must be false. true means the narration_text is the article prose read aloud with no listening-structure recompilation — the default failure this contract exists to prevent.

structural_changes.description: What changed between article prose and spoken script (reordering, compression, recurrence added, transitions rewritten).

render.description: Rendering lineage only (provider/model/version/voice) — never editorial state. Nullable because a plan below the render gate has not rendered yet.

script_l1.description: L1 spoken-naturalness review (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §20 'Script QA'). Cheap preflight that must pass before an expensive render (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §9).

segments.description: Semantic segment plan (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §17). Segment boundaries are chosen by meaning first, then fit to provider limits.

spoken_script.description: The canonical narration_text SSOT (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §2). Clean spoken text only — never provider markup, stage directions, or delivery instructions.

schema.title: Audio Plan

alignment_evidence.description: The evidence_ref is an alignment-evidence://sha256 content address computed from audio_ref, audio_sha256, and segments; the StageResult must list that exact output ref.

engine_stage_result.description: shorts_gen StageResult schema 1.0.0, scoped to completed qa_repair alignment verification.

schema.title: Video BGM Catalog v2

value.description: Artifact profile id, namespaced by modality: `text/article`, `visual/body-infographic`, `audio/dialogue`. The modality prefix is what keeps text, visual, and audio generation contracts separate.

audience_axis.description: Audience is the one axis shared by every modality: it changes explanation depth in text, information density in visuals, and pace and assumed knowledge in audio. A preset plus task-specific trait overrides, never a rigid bucket.

traits.description: Task-specific deviations from the preset. Only traits that materially change delivery belong here — demographics that change nothing are ceremonial and are omitted.

life_stage.description: Recorded only when it materially affects communication — a child audience changes vocabulary and example choice; an age number that changes nothing does not belong here.

basis.description: Why this value. For `confirmed`, the span of the utterance or the upstream contract that fixed it. For `assumed`, the inference. Required in practice for audit; a value with no basis cannot be routed when it turns out wrong.

profile_ref.description: Repository path of the resolved profile. Absent when unresolved.

value.description: Profile id within the matching axis directory under editorial/profiles/. null only when state is missing_material.

options.description: Choices with a marked default beat an open prompt. A clarification with no options is a defect unless the field genuinely has an open range.

reference_input.description: Material that can inform craft. Carries no factual authority: an evaluation of a reference may never become a verified claim.

dimensions.description: Which dimensions of this reference the human actually wants applied. `이 reference는 정보 구조는 좋은데 색감은 싫어` becomes dimensions plus a task override, not wholesale imitation.

resolution_state.description: confirmed: the human said it, or an authoritative upstream contract did — the only state that may inform durable calibration. assumed: safely inferred for this run; never durable preference evidence. missing_material: absent and materially outcome-changing.

source_input.description: Material that can establish fact. Referenced by id and never copied into this repository.

schema.description: The structured result of natural-language intake (AES-V2.1 / SUE-559) expressed over five independent axes (AES-V2.2 / SUE-560). A human writes sentences; an agent writes this. Every axis value carries a resolution state, and only `confirmed` values may ever inform durable calibration.

axes.description: The five independent axes. They do not collapse into one another: a transformation is not a content type, a surface is not an audience, an artifact is not a style.

artifacts.description: One or more requested artifacts. Empty means the artifact axis is still unresolved and must appear in clarification.required.

calibration_ref.description: The calibration version active at intake (AES-V2.10). Recorded so a later verdict can be attributed to the calibration that produced it rather than to whichever is current.

clarification.description: The exception path. Questions are asked only when a missing field would materially change thesis, audience fit, transformation fidelity, artifact route, publication constraint, or cost.

asked.description: Normally 0-3 entries. An intake that asks four or more questions has failed its own gate and must record why in `note`.

required.description: Axis or constraint paths currently in state `missing_material`. Non-empty forces status `blocked_on_clarification`.

resolution.description: proceeded: nothing material was missing. answered: the human supplied the missing values. default_authorized: the human said `알아서 해` / `use default`, which authorizes `assumed` for this run and nothing beyond it. unresolved: still blocked.

max_source_age_days.description: Freshness ceiling when the request is time-sensitive. Absent means the content-type profile decides.

inputs.description: Source and Reference are separate lists because they are separate kinds of authority. A reference can never establish a fact; a source can never dictate a composition.

intent_id.description: Stable id for this intake. Lineage anchor: every downstream frame, plan, artifact, and feedback record cites it.

overrides.description: Values the human set for THIS RUN only. Task-scoped by construction — an override is never durable preference, and V2.10 calibration may not read this array.

request.description: What the human actually said, kept verbatim. The intake is auditable only if the utterance survives next to its interpretation.

language.description: BCP-47 language of the request itself. Not the output language — that is constraints.output_language.

received_by.description: Agent runtime that performed intake, e.g. `claude-code`, `chatgpt`. Recorded so an intake defect can be attributed.

status.description: ready: the intent may drive framing/planning. blocked_on_clarification: at least one material field is unresolved. declined: intake refused the request and recorded why in clarification.note.

schema.title: Editorial Intent

lineage.description: Consistent with the V1 staleness rule (ARTICLE-ARTIFACT-CONTRACT.md): claims_hash unchanged means cosmetic drift, changed means material drift and dependent artifacts are stale.

claims_hash.description: sha256 over the ordered verified-claim set (id, text, status) — same convention as article.schema.json#/$defs/version/properties/claims_hash. When article_ref is set, must equal article_ref.claims_hash: the package does not compute a second claims_hash for claims it does not hold. null only when this package carries no claims at all (e.g. a pure translate/adapt of non-factual material).

package_hash.description: sha256 over this package's own normalised content (everything except this lineage block). Lets a consumer detect a changed package without a diff.

produced_by.description: Vendor-neutral: a Skill is the orchestration contract, the tool is a replaceable worker. `tool` carries the same full runtime-lineage shape as visual-job.schema.json's `renderer` block (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §7 model-drift contract) rather than a second spelling of it — a package's writer/framer identity is exactly as detectable as its renderer's.

tool.description: Full runtime lineage. Field names deliberately match visual-job.schema.json's `renderer`/`runtime` $defs: tool/tool_version identify the compiling pipeline; provider/model/model_version identify the generative runtime, and are still recorded for a deterministic tool as the tool's own identity so the field is never blank.

source_ref.description: Reference and provenance only — mirrors source.schema.json identity fields. No field here can carry a source body.

schema.description: The destination-neutral handoff object for AES-V2.9 (SUE-567). Carries the minimum reusable semantics of one verified body of work — enough for it to reach several surfaces (suengj.com, NotebookLM, an academic export, a promotional channel) without duplicating source truth or the Article contract. Not an Article: where an Article already exists, this package cites it by `article_ref` rather than copying its frame or claims. See schemas/EDITORIAL-PACKAGE-CONTRACT.md for the rules this schema cannot express.

approved_artifacts.description: Artifact ids a human has approved for handoff to an adapter.

article_ref.description: Set when a V1 Article already carries the verified frame and claims this package draws on. Same shape as artifact.schema.json#/$defs/article_ref. When set, thesis/key_concepts/summary/verified_claims are null/empty on this package — the article is cited, not copied. null when there is no article (a package that exists because no Article was warranted, e.g. a P03 summarize-to-note).

calibration_ref.description: The calibration version active when this package's content was produced. Same pattern as editorial-intent.schema.json#/properties/calibration_ref.

intent_ref.description: The `intent_id` of the editorial-intent record this package fulfils. Same pattern as editorial-intent.schema.json#/properties/intent_id — the package is downstream of intake, never a second intake.

package_id.description: Stable identity. Lineage anchor for downstream adapters and feedback.

proposed_artifacts.description: Artifact ids this package could still produce, namespaced by modality so text/visual/audio/video generation contracts stay separate.

reference_profile_refs.description: Which reference material's craft evidence was active while this package's content was produced. Never a factual source — see V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md section 2.

rights.description: Carries forward source.schema.json's rights fields and article.schema.json's transformation record rather than inventing a third rights model. Optional: a package built entirely from original, unsourced synthesis may omit it.

transcript_shaped.description: Same meaning as article.schema.json#/$defs/transformation/properties/transcript_shaped. True blocks handoff to any adapter — see the contract doc.

sources.description: Refs and provenance only. Never a source body — enforced structurally: this object has no field capable of holding one.

summary.description: One self-contained compression, capped like the Article AnswerUnit so it stays a summary rather than a second article.

target_surfaces.description: A package may legitimately serve more than one surface — that is the reason it exists instead of an Article. Non-empty is a validator rule (json-schema-lite cannot express minItems).

thesis.description: Required (non-null) when this package is the sole carrier of a new argument — synthesize/original with no article_ref. null when article_ref is set (the article's frame.thesis is the thesis) or when the transformation does not produce one (extract, translate).

transformation.description: What this package's content may claim to have done to its sources. Semantics live in editorial/profiles/transformation/<value>.json (owned there, not here) — this field only names and points at the profile.

uncertainty.description: What is not known. May not be empty for synthesize/original packages — a validator rule (schemas/EDITORIAL-PACKAGE-CONTRACT.md), not expressible here.

verified_claims.description: Same field names and semantics as article.schema.json#/$defs/verification/properties/claims — the same contract expressed at package scope, never a second claim model. Empty when article_ref is set: the claims live in the article and are cited via lineage.claims_hash, not restated here.

schema.title: Editorial Package

routing.description: Which layer (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5) produced the failure or success this feedback names. Abstention must be expressible: layer null with abstained true says the record could not tell rather than guessing.

abstained.description: True when this record cannot name a layer with confidence.

modality_layer.description: Modality-specific routing detail, e.g. a TEXT/VISUAL/AUDIO sub-concern. Free text; the shared layer above is the enumerated one.

schema.description: One append-only record of human or agent feedback on a generated output (AES-V2.3 / SUE-561). Distinct from a reference evaluation: this judges what the system produced, not third-party material. See docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5 (layers) and §6 (four separate signals, never averaged).

basis.description: explicit_human_feedback: the human said it. model_inference: an agent judged it.

evidence_links.description: Ids of other feedback or evaluation records this one corroborates. Required (non-empty) when scope is calibration_candidate — a single record, human- or agent-authored, never promotes itself; it must point at the repeated independent evidence it joins. AES-V2.10 still owns the actual promotion.

owner_verdict.description: Distinct from verdict: whether the owner actually accepted the output, not the evaluator's read of its quality. unknown is the required default when no owner acceptance/rejection has actually been expressed — it is never omitted and never inferred as accepted from publication, an L1 pass, silence, or time passing.

scope.description: task_local (the safe default) or calibration_candidate. A single record may never be calibration_candidate on its own basis alone — see references/REFERENCE-EVALUATION-PROTOCOL.md and AES-V2.10, which owns promotion into durable calibration.

signal.description: The four V2 signals stay separate and are never averaged into one score.

statement.description: What the human actually said, verbatim where possible.

ref.description: Id or path of the generated thing this feedback is about.

schema.title: Feedback record

schema.description: A reviewer-produced, card-hash-bound check for exact embedded strings, logos, and deterministic chrome. This is not visual approval or publication authority.

claim_set.description: Authoritative article claim identity. The article_ref claims_hash binds this declared set to the upstream article version.

information_hierarchy.description: Integrated reader hierarchy that must remain coherent with the selected reference authority.

publication_display_surfaces.description: Authoritative publication-display geometry for the full and mobile surfaces. These are RenderSpec declarations, not review assertions.

text_ownership.description: The three V2.17 ownership classes. Verified generative facts carry a canonical payload, source lineage, and mandatory post-render verification.

verified_generative_fact.description: Null explicitly represents that this ownership class has no items; an object declares generated facts that require authoritative payload lineage and post-render verification.

watermark.description: Optional, default-OFF deterministic watermark overlay on a flattened PNG (SUE-1303). Every field is optional so a profile default, a RenderSpec, and an account/channel override can each set only what they change; omitted fields resolve to the defaults in scripts/lib/watermark-core.mjs (enabled=false). Glyphs are composited by the renderer, never drawn by an image model. This is not the accidental-watermark detection in editorial/IMAGE-GENERATION.md.

enabled.description: Defaults to false (OFF). OFF is a byte-identical no-op.

exclusion_zones.description: Layout-declared regions (numbers, charts, small text) the watermark must not touch, as image fractions. If the watermark box intersects one, the derivative is not produced.

placement.description: Horizontal placements only. Diagonal is deliberately not allowed: it crosses content, which the exclusion-zone rule forbids.

safe_margins.description: Fractions of image height (bottom) and width (left/right).

scale.description: Font size as a fraction of image width.

crop_anchors.description: Semantic anchors that a publication crop may preserve. Review records may select only one of these declared anchors.

profile.purpose: Explain verified source material through a compact learning sequence.
Present source-grounded choices or states in a declared sequence, side by side, or combined hybrid.
Explain source-grounded material with canonical narration synchronized to scene and beat identities.

dark-data.generation_direction: High-contrast dark editorial composition with restrained mint accents. Illustration supports rather than competes with evidence. Never invent KPI tiles, chart marks, performance percentages, or product brands.

editorial-minimal.generation_direction: Restrained magazine composition; generous negative space; one clear subject; quiet material texture. No ornamental mini dashboards or icon grids. Typography remains in reserved compositor regions.

theme.font_family: 'Noto Serif CJK KR', 'Noto Serif KR', Georgia, serif

pop-collage.generation_direction: Expressive paper collage with pink/orange/blue accents, torn edges, playful brush texture and one dominant silhouette. Restrict collage to its supplied content slot; no factual copy, faux numbers, logos, robot cliches or unrelated slogans unless specifically requested.

r4-photo-fullbleed.generation_direction: R4 owner-preferred photo-led editorial direction. Use the supplied strong source photo as the full-bleed visual whenever present, preserving the original pixels and recording crop/focal-point decisions. Keep factual text in the existing deterministic compositor regions. Do not replace a suitable photo with generated illustration. If a usable photo is absent or weak, resolve to R7 before rendering.

theme.font_family: 'Noto Sans KR', 'Noto Sans CJK KR', sans-serif

r7-illustration-fallback.generation_direction: R7 owner-preferred illustration fallback for weak or absent photo assets, and for lifestyle/practical-information content. Use one centered, large subject with clean color blocks and restrained highlighter accents. Keep all exact text, numbers, citations and labels in the deterministic compositor; never render them into the illustration.

theme.font_family: 'Noto Sans KR', 'Noto Sans CJK KR', sans-serif

recipes.scope: Task-selected realization presets, not a new intent axis or a replacement brand/reference authority. No factual payload or approval.
